boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten campus places with documented uses for studying, making, gathering, recreation, cultural exchange and quiet breaks.

cards.title: Build Your Own Study Setup at Hale
cards.subtitle: Private nooks, collaboration rooms and computer stations
cards.notes: Choose a private nook for solo work, or reserve a collaboration room when your group needs a display and shared workspace.
cards.short_summary: A central library where students can switch between individual focus, group work and computer access.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State Libraries says Hale Library provides private study nooks, reservable collaboration rooms with digital displays, computer stations and a graduate hub.
cards.access_notes: Library spaces are available during posted building hours; some rooms require reservations, and the Grad Hub is restricted to graduate students.

cards.title: Take Quiet Work to the Great Room
cards.subtitle: A designated quiet room on Hale Library’s third floor
cards.notes: Bring individual work to the third-floor Great Room, keep conversation elsewhere and use the room’s quiet-study designation.
cards.short_summary: Historic architecture and a formal quiet policy make this a distinct alternative to Hale’s collaborative floors.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State Libraries identifies the Great Room on Hale Library’s third floor as a designated quiet-study area with abundant study space.
cards.access_notes: Located on the northwest side of Hale Library’s third floor; follow the posted quiet-area expectations.

cards.title: Prototype Something in the Innovation Lab
cards.subtitle: Hale Library tools for making and media work
cards.notes: Start at the lab when a project needs prototyping or media tools, and review its equipment-specific safety rules before working.
cards.short_summary: A shared making environment for turning class and personal ideas into physical or digital projects.
cards.evidence_claim: The lab’s official policy states that it supports collaborative learning, experimentation, prototyping and community building and is open to students and community members.
cards.access_notes: Open to K-State students, faculty, staff and community members; hazardous areas have additional supervision and safety requirements.

cards.title: Use the Union Beyond the Food Court
cards.subtitle: Lounges, student programs and recreation under one roof
cards.notes: Check the floor directory for lounges, student-program offices and the lower-level recreation spaces before choosing where to meet.
cards.short_summary: The Union combines everyday gathering space with student organizations, services, events and recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: The university campus-map page describes the Union as a student-life hub containing student-organization offices, retail and dining options, and a bowling alley.
cards.source_title: K-State Campus Map: K-State Student Union
cards.access_notes: Individual businesses, offices, events and recreation facilities may have separate hours, eligibility rules or charges.

cards.title: Meet Across Cultures at the International Student Center
cards.subtitle: A social and cultural gathering place near the north campus residences
cards.notes: Look for a public program or use the center’s relaxed setting to connect with international students and campus organizations.
cards.short_summary: A purpose-built campus setting for social connection and programs that foster cultural awareness.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State’s campus-map page says the International Student Center offers international students a comfortable atmosphere for socializing and has hosted cultural-awareness events.
cards.source_title: K-State Campus Map: International Student Center
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to the center’s current building schedule and any event-specific participation requirements.

cards.title: Turn a Group Plan Into a Meeting
cards.subtitle: Classrooms, conference rooms and event space
cards.notes: Use the building for informal coordination, or submit a reservation request when your class, meeting or event needs a dedicated room.
cards.short_summary: A teaching building that also supports meetings, conferences and student-led events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Staley School says the Leadership Studies Building serves as an educational facility and offers reservable classrooms, conference rooms and a lecture hall.
cards.access_notes: The cited page lists weekday building hours and requires reservations for formal use of rooms; university closures apply.

cards.title: Find Collaborative Space at the Multicultural Center
cards.subtitle: An all-campus hub for intercultural learning
cards.notes: Drop in during building hours to learn about the center, then ask staff about meeting, reflection or student-organization spaces.
cards.short_summary: An open-to-all center where cultural learning and student collaboration share the same home.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State identifies the Morris Family Multicultural Student Center as an open-to-all hub for intercultural learning and collaborative initiatives.
cards.access_notes: Open to all; consult the page for current seasonal hours and contact staff about reserving specialized spaces.

cards.entity_name: Marianna Kistler Beach Museum of Art Atrium
cards.title: Reset or Study in the Museum Atrium
cards.subtitle: A bring-your-own-lunch space beside the galleries
cards.notes: Bring a snack or a small study task to the Atrium, then use a gallery walk as a deliberate break between work sessions.
cards.short_summary: A museum seating area designed for both quiet study and relaxed time with friends.
cards.evidence_claim: The Beach Museum says its Atrium is available for studying or relaxation and welcomes visitors to bring lunch or a snack; admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Use the Atrium during posted museum hours; the museum is closed Sundays, Mondays and university holidays.

cards.title: Take a Walking Break Through the Gardens
cards.subtitle: Open-air collections on Denison Avenue
cards.notes: Walk the garden paths between classes and scan the student-created interpretive signs when you want context for the plantings.
cards.short_summary: A free campus landscape for a daylight break, informal observation or a slow walk with classmates.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gardens’ official page states that the grounds are open daily with free admission and features student-created interpretive signs throughout the site.
cards.source_title: Kansas State University Gardens: Events & News
cards.access_notes: Grounds are open daily during the posted garden hours; the visitor center follows a separate weekday schedule.

cards.entity_name: Paul Weigel Library of Architecture, Planning and Design
cards.title: Work in Weigel’s Design-Focused Setting
cards.subtitle: Quiet seating and workspaces inside Regnier Hall
cards.notes: Use Weigel for quiet work and design references, then move into the adjoining Pierce Information Commons for a meeting.
cards.short_summary: A smaller branch library pairing specialized design collections with natural light and quiet work areas.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State Libraries says Weigel Library is open to everyone, provides quiet study seating and workspaces, and adjoins the Pierce Information Commons.
cards.access_notes: Located in room 0081 Regnier Hall; when Regnier is closed, use the entrance from the William T. Kemper Foundation Amphitheatre.
